title: NM Parole Board Member Terms & Salaries

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: NM Parole Board Member Terms & Salaries
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

-the current term expiration date (month, day, and year) for each parole board member
-the annual salary / total compensation for each parole board member for 2026

I am making this request for research purposes and am not a journalist.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Wourms

Jacob Wourms 

 
Re: Request to Inspect Public Records - Production
 
Dear Mr. Wourms:
 
On October 21, 2026, we received your request to inspect:
 
The following records : 
 
-the current term expiration date (month, day, and year) for each parole board member
-the annual salary / total compensation for each parole board member for 2026

 
We are providing the records that are responsive to your request. Please note in all documents produced, personal identifying information has been redacted including months and days of birth, Social Security numbers, tax identification numbers, driver’s license numbers, and financial account numbers of relatives pursuant to Sections 14-2-1.1 and 14-2-6(E), NMSA 1978.  Personal or home addresses and phone numbers have also been redacted within the provided documents pursuant to Section 14-2-6(G) (Record must relate to public business to be defined as a public record) and the Attorney General’s Inspection of Public Records Act Compliance Guide, Ninth Edition, pages 32-33 (Agency can deny a request for personal contact information because the record does not relate to public business, as it does not reveal anything about the official acts of the employees or the operations or activities of the agency). The Records below were withheld pursuant to Records relating to medical and mental health diagnoses are protected from disclosure by the Inspection of Public Records Act and the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and have therefore been withheld.  NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1(A) and 14-2-6; State ex rel. Newsome v. Alarid, 1977-NMSC-076, ¶ 11, 90 N.M. 790, 794; NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1(H); 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(a)(1) and 164.512(e)(1). Please note that, pursuant to NMSA 1978, § 14-6-1, as well as IPRA caselaw, Meyer v. Regents of Univ. of New Mexico, A-1-CA-4097, 2024 WL 3311335, par. 16, medical records are not public records. As such, they cannot be released under IPRA, lest they become public records, and result in our violating HIPAA (irrespective of any medical release)

“All social records, including presentence reports, pre-parole reports and supervision histories, obtained by the board are privileged and shall not be disclosed directly or indirectly” to the public.  NMSA 1978, § 31-21-6.  These records are also protected by a policy adopted by the Secretary of the Corrections Department.  NMSA 1978, §§ 9-3-5(E) and 33-1-6(B) (authority to adopt rules for Department operation); CD-040101(C)(1)(g)(2)-(3).  The records are therefore exempt from public inspection and are being withheld.  NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1(H).  Pre-Parole reports obtained by the Parole Board are privileged and may not be released to any non-Correctional Department personnel, including the inmate and/or his attorney, without permission of the Parole Board.

NCIC arrest and fingerprint records from the provided materials are being withheld.  NCIC records are confidential pursuant to United States Dept. of Justice v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, 489 U.S. 749, 757-758, 780, 109 S.Ct. 1468, 1474, 1485 (1989); 28 U.S.C..]
 

1.	Current roster held by the office of Michelle Lujan Grisham, Boards and Commission 
2.   Current payment for per diem for board members from January to current. all members are volunteers and do not receive salary compensation. 

With this production and explanation, we consider your request closed. If you believe a record exists that was not provided to you, please let us know at the earliest opportunity.

Respectfully


Roberta Cohen
Executive Director
New Mexico Adult Parole Board

title: Clearview AI: Contracts, Purchases, Vendor Contacts, and Communications (City of Savannah)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Clearview AI: Contracts, Purchases, Vendor Contacts, and Communications (City of Savannah)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any contract, order form, quote, proposal, terms of service, renewal, amendment, or sole-source or procurement justification between the City of Savannah (including the Savannah Police Department) and Clearview AI, Inc. (City Vendor #25565), including the version of the Clearview Terms of Service that applied to each purchase.

2. Purchase and payment records for Clearview AI purchases dated after January 2, 2025, including requisitions, quotes, approvals, purchase orders, invoices, payment records, the service period each invoice covers, and documents showing the budget unit or funding source charged. This includes PO 306567 and Invoice INV-10821 (paid July 3, 2025, charged to unit 102.4122) and PO 50041 and Invoice INV-11697 (paid May 1, 2026). Please also include the requisition, quote, and approval records for PO 115455 (February 7, 2024), if they exist.

3. The vendor registration or setup file for Clearview AI, Inc. (Vendor #25565), including the vendor application, W-9, and contact information for Clearview representatives. Bank account details may be redacted.

4. Email metadata only (sender, all recipients including cc and bcc, subject line, and date and time) for any email to or from an address at the clearview.ai domain in any City email account, from January 1, 2023 through the date of this request, including messages involving Roberto Gomez or Patrick Schoenberg. Please also include calendar metadata (title, date and time, and attendees) for any meeting, call, or demonstration with Clearview.

5. Records of any review or approval of these purchases beyond Purchasing, such as an Information Technology Services security review, a privacy or data-protection assessment, or City Manager or Council approval.
6. 
Documents sufficient to show whether any City department other than the Police Department has purchased, licensed, or trialed Clearview AI.

These records are likely held by Procurement and Contracts, Information Technology Services, and the Police Department; please search each. If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d) provides, and produce all reasonably segregable portions. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right to Know Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ICE Death Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

ICE detainee death records for Julio Cesar Chirino Peralta, a 32 year-old migrant from Nicaragua, who died following his detention at the Port Isabel Detention Center on October 8, 2023 (see https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrJulioCesarChirinoPeralta.pdf): 

1. The Office of Professional Responsibility Detainee Death Review (search the External Reviews and Analysis Unit within ICE OPR); 
2. The Creative Corrections Healthcare and Security Compliance Analysis report (search ERAU); 
3. the IHSC Mortality Review (search the ICE Health Service Corps); 
4. The IHSC Root Cause Analysis, if any (search IHSC). 

We request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and provide the following statements in support of our request under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746: 

1. At the time of this request, ICE deaths in custody have doubled the highest levels from previous years of the Biden administration. https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-double-last-year-rcna154659#:~:text=NBC%20News%20Tipline-,The%20number%20of%20deaths%20in%20ICE%20custody%20is%20already%20more,of%20the%20six%20preceding%20years.
2. The current rate of in-custody ICE deaths is on track to exceed any non-COVID year since FY17. See: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11007418/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7870381/
3. Deaths in ICE custody have been the subject of widespread, ongoing media coverage and extensive policy advocacy and discussion. See, e.g. ,https://www.npr.org/2023/11/08/1211316303/ice-releases-investigation-into-immigrants-death-after-months-of-inexcusable-del; https://www.yahoo.com/news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-133000592.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAALCThkPLfU2ufNLo_I3yqmeUO38qEyUSI4U597M71FTc3npyfor0xVw-REfCt-2anUv5517ufGPQZZuU4KKiJ98axkk_ivGQf5e9Gu_gYZaHzjunplOd3-7tEQTfDoPBn6g0zjNvYt8aKSYJBBN9iLv2gvnes6k94yMIMemD-0yw; https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/30/us/migrant-death-ice-custody-recommended-release/index.html.
4. There exist serious questions regarding the government's capacity to ensure safe and humane detention conditions that prevent deaths in ICE custody, based on available FOIA records obtained through federal litigation.  See, e.g., https://prismreports.org/2023/04/20/ice-gourgan-mirimanian-death-2018/; https://today.usc.edu/ice-deaths-custody-detention-medical-standards-violated-usc-study/
5. ICE has announced its intention to expand its detention system, potentially increasing the numbers of in-custody death to even higher levels. https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/ice-announces-ongoing-work-optimize-enforcement-resources
6. ICE has previously failed to accurately inform the public of its own internal agency conclusions about the events leading up to in-custody deaths. See, e.g., https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/April-2024-ACLU-Letter-to-ICE-on-Torrance-Detention-Facility.pdf

There is a compelling need to obtain these records as soon as possible so that the public can understand the consequences of ICE's current detention management processes as the agency seeks to expand the system beyond its appropriated limit of 41,500 beds.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2024-ICFO-41781 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your 6/16/2024, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for records pertaining to the death of Julio Cesar Chirino Peralta.  Your request was received in this office on 6/16/2024. 

Some information has already been made public at chrome-extension://efaidnbmnnnibpcajpcglclefindmkaj/https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrJulioCesarChirinoPeralta.pdf and at https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/nicaraguan-national-ice-custody-dies. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations, as they apply to media requesters.  As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2024-ICFO-41781. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely,

communications.subject: North Dakota Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Public Records Request — Minnesota Generative AI Records

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Public Records Request — Minnesota Generative AI Records
communications.communication:
Subject: Public Records Request — AI Chatbot Interaction Logs

April 9, 2026

Data Practices Compliance Official
Minnesota IT Services (MNIT)
658 Cedar Street
St. Paul, MN 55155

Dear Data Practices Compliance Official,

I am writing on behalf of a team of researchers and journalists from Stanford University, the University of Southern California, KNKX Public Radio and the New York Times. We are studying how government agencies are adopting and using AI tools in their daily work.

We are writing to request records related to Minnesota's use of generative AI tools by state employees, including Microsoft Copilot Chat and the nebulaONE chatbot platform.

We are requesting the following records under Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3:

1. All interaction logs from Microsoft 365 Government Copilot Chat, nebulaONE, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, or any other generative AI chatbot tool — including prompts submitted by state employees and responses generated by the AI — for the period from April 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. We request these records in their native electronic format where available (e.g., HTML exports, JSON, or CSV).

2. Any policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, or training materials governing state employee use of Microsoft Copilot Chat, nebulaONE, or other generative AI chatbot tools.

3. Any data retention or deletion policies applicable to AI chatbot interaction logs, including any schedules for automatic deletion of interaction data.

4. Administrative usage statistics for Microsoft Copilot Chat and nebulaONE showing number of users, sessions, and queries processed.

We are seeking the substantive content of AI interactions for research purposes. We do not need personally identifying information of individual employees (such as names and email addresses).

Minnesota was one of the first states to roll out Microsoft 365 Government Copilot Chat to executive branch employees at no cost as part of its existing Microsoft contract, beginning April 8, 2025 (see GovTech, "Minnesota Taps Free GenAI Through Microsoft Partnership," https://www.govtech.com/biz/minnesota-taps-free-genai-through-microsoft-partnership). All prompts, responses, and content remain within the Microsoft Government Community Cloud (GCC) environment. Additionally, MNIT is advancing the nebulaONE chatbot development tool with support from the Technology Modernization Fund and Microsoft investment funds to enable safe deployment of AI-powered services including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and custom chatbots (see MNIT, "Empowering State Employees with Secure, AI-Driven Tools," https://mn.gov/mnit/about-mnit/tmf/state-employee-ai-chat-bot-tools.jsp).

We note that records of this type have been made available in response to public records requests in other jurisdictions. See Cascade PBS, "WA City Officials Are Using ChatGPT to Write Government Documents" (Aug. 2025), https://www.cascadepbs.org/news/2025/08/wa-city-officials-are-using-chatgpt-to-write-government-documents/; see also Texas State AI Usage — Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), MuckRock, https://www.muckrock.com/foi/texas-109/texas-state-ai-usage-texas-department-of-transportation-txdot-196227/#files.

The results of this research will be published in peer-reviewed academic venues and will contribute to public understanding of how public servants interact with AI systems. This request is made by an academic research institution for scholarly, non-commercial purposes; as such, we request a fee waiver or reduction. If a fee waiver is not granted, please inform me of estimated costs before proceeding. I am willing to pay fees up to $20.

I understand that this may be a novel type of records request and I am happy to answer any technical questions. Please feel free to contact me at the email address below.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Alexander Spangher
Postdoctoral Researcher
Stanford University
alexspan@stanford.edu

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that ChatGPT conversation histories can be exported by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. For Microsoft Copilot, interaction histories may be available through the Microsoft 365 admin console or the Purview compliance center. For Google Gemini, interaction data may be available through Google Vault or Google Takeout. We are happy to provide additional technical guidance if that would be helpful.

P.P.S. The Minnesota Government Data Practices Act covers all "government data," defined as all data collected, created, received, maintained, or disseminated by a government entity regardless of physical form. Minn. Stat. § 13.02, subd. 7. Governor Walz's Executive Order 24-03 (2024) directed state agencies to develop policies for responsible AI use, including transparency and accountability provisions. Minnesota IT Services (MNIT) has issued guidance requiring that AI-generated content used in official business be treated as government data subject to existing retention schedules. Consistent with this trend nationally, NARA has made clear that chats and other electronic messages used for agency business are likely government records. NARA Bulletin 2023-02 (Jan. 5, 2023), https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins/2023/2023-02.

Good morning,

This email acknowledges your data request to Minnesota IT Services.

I am MNIT’s Data Practices Compliance Official and I will be working with you in regards to the MNIT data that is associated with your request. I wanted to let you know the cost will be significantly higher than $20. Under Minn. Stat. <https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.03> §13.03, subd. 3(c), MNIT is authorized to charge a fee to recover the costs associated with searching, compiling, and sending the information that you have requested. The cost of employee time to search for and retrieve data is based on the lowest paid employee who is able to execute the search and retrieval. The cost estimate is calculated using the lowest paid employee’s hourly wage and fringe pay. Given the large amount of data you are requesting the cost of this will likely be over $100 and will require prepayment. Are you still interested in the data? If so, I can work on getting you an exact cost estimate.

Please also note that I can only provide you with MNIT data, we cannot provide you with agency data. If you want data from a specific agency you will need to make a data request to that agency.

Please reach out if you have questions and to let me know if you would like me to proceed with getting you an exact cost estimate.

Thanks,

Katie Pauk

Sorry for the delay. So just to confirm, it will be $411 + reviewing costs? Do you have an estimate for the reviewing costs?

Just to give you some background, we are researchers and our primary goal is to assess:
    (1) how are AI systems being used in government
    (2) what kinds of future directions should academia take to (1) build benchmarks (2) conduct methodological research in order to improve AI tooling for government.
We are very much hoping that these efforts can produce AI models that better meet the needs of government employees and ultimately members of the public.

We are seeking substantive volumes of records from varied roles at MNIT:
  - Technical/IT staff (developers, system administrators, engineers)
  - Program/project management
  - Legal/counsel
  - Administrative/executive support
  - Senior leadership, or any Policy/regulatory staff who might exist at MNIT
  - Budget/finance/procurement
  - Communications

If it is constructive to filter down to 10% or 5% of the users currently in the 2,800 users, as long as they are evenly distributed across these roles, we would accept that constraint.

We are very amenable to receiving anonymized data. We have no interest in identifying specific people. We are simply interested in analyzing this data and generating aggregated benchmarking around use-cases.

Alex

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Flock audit - large search access August 2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the following ID's of Flock Search records from Renton PD, I would like to get information on: 

- Number of results returned to the officer for this search.
- Count of the number of images that were accessed by the officer for this search.
- Number of images which were accessed from Renton's 24 camera Flock network, versus external to Renton's network.
- Description of images accessed by the officer (license plate, car make, model, camera location, etc)

For reference, this is the Renton PD ALPR page which implies there is a method to determine a number of images accessed for searches ( https://www.rentonwa.gov/Government/Departments-and-Offices/Police/Police-Transparency/Automated-License-Plate-Readers  Section: Searches )

Flock Search ID:
09650265-6932-4a98-95a1-55d3d1bc6b29

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian Hughes

    Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following
    records:
    
    A copy of file 321D-IR-A7788.
    
    The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and

    In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me

    Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look

    as the statute requires.

communications.subject: (U) USSOCOM 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, 2026-289 and 2026-392 - Acknowledgements
communications.communication:
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Message Body Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Dear Ms. Best,

This is in response to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request (copy attached) you submitted to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and it was subsequently referred to U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).  It was assigned USSOCOM FOIA 2026-392.  In addition, the FBI previously referred documents to USSOCOM to review pertaining to this request, and they were assigned as USSOCOM FOIA control numbers 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, and 2026-289.  We apologize that you did not receive acknowledgements from us previously for these other case numbers.  Please refer to these numbers should you have any questions concerning your request.

Your requests are being processed in accordance with procedural requirements promulgated in Department of Defense (DoD) Manual 5400.07, which is available on the internet at: https://open.defense.gov/Portals/23/Documents/FOIA/FOIA_Resources/DoDM%205400.07.pdf?ver=2017-03-15-135646-847.  The actual processing time will depend upon its complexity, whether it involves sensitive records, voluminous records, extensive searches, consultation among DoD components or other agencies, and our administrative workload.

We have placed you in the "News Media" category for fee purposes, which means you are obligated to pay for any duplication costs after the first 100 pages; however, depending on the size of the documents, we may provide the final releases on CD or electronically and no charges would be applicable.

The USSOCOM FOIA Office has a substantial number of pending FOIA cases; therefore, we process requests in a multi-track processing system based on the date of receipt and the amount of work and time involved in processing each request.  We estimate the time for completion to be approximately 4-6 months; it could be more or less.  If you wish to discuss this or have any other questions or concerns, please contact this office at FOIA@socom.mil<mailto:FOIA@socom.mil>.
Regards,
USSOCOM FOIA Team




Attachment Classification: UNCLASSIFIED
Message Body Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Pacific Coast Intermodal Port (PCIP) Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP) FY 2026 Grant Application
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

As it relates to the Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP), FY2026 round "Pacific Coast Intermodal Port (PCIP) Terminal Connection Project," Coos Bay, Oregon (awarded $11,250,000):**

a. The complete grant application as submitted, including all attachments, exhibits, and appendices
b. The advance grant notice
c. The executed Grant Agreement, including any amendments
d. The scoring and review records for the FY2026 PIDP round as they pertain to this application: the scoring rubric/criteria, individual reviewer score sheets and written comments, the applicant ranking table, and any interagency or technical review memoranda.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Wyn Manselle

communications.subject: South Carolina Public Records Law Request: FOIA Request: Flock Audits
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Carolina Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The data logged from the period of July 1, 2026 to July 30, 2026. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency. The data should include all selectable columns.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The data logged from the period of July 1, 2026 to July 30, 2026. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System. The data should include all selectable columns.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days for records less than 24-months-old, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

m

Thank you for your interest in public records of Spokane County. Your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with the State of Washington Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW. Your request was received in this office on 5/12/2026 and given the reference number S028935-051226 for tracking purposes. Spokane County Sheriff provides access to public records in compliance with applicable laws and statutes of the State of Washington. In accordance with the public records law, the Sheriff's office has five business days to respond to a request for public records. Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

A list of non-city-owned devices, such as cameras, automatic license plate readers, and gunshot detection systems, registered and/or integrated with the Sheriff's Office's Fusus Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) system through the CONNECT SPOKANE COUNTY program (https://connectspokanecounty.org/) sufficient to discern the registration name, full street address, number of internal and external devices, whether devices are registered or integrated, and date/time created.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Rose Terse 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2287620/ 
Not all public documents are available in electronic format. If the document(s) requested are not available electronically, we will make them available for inspection or by paper copy in accordance with the Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW. 
 
Your request will be forwarded to the relevant department(s) to locate the information you seek and to determine the volume and any costs associated with satisfying your request. You will be contacted about the availability and/or provided with copies of the records in question. PLEASE NOTE: The State of Washington Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW, does not require a governmental body to create new information, to do legal research, or to answer questions. 
 
You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you'll receive an email when your request has been completed. 
 
Please be advised that Spokane Regional Emergency Communications ("SREC") is the custodian of 911 and Crime Check audio recordings as well as audio recordings of dispatch and radio traffic. Spokane County

communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Wourms,
This is not a request for documents under the Freedom of Access Act. Instead, it is a list of questions directed to a state agency, which FOAA does not provide for.

To try to assist you, I have attached the report available online from the Maine Secretary of State that shows the current members of the parole board.

You may search for additional information on boards like the parole board there: https://www.maine.gov/sos/corporations-commissions/commissions/boards-and-commissions.

Compensation for boards and commissions is governed by statute, specifically 5 M.R.S. chapter 379 (Boards, Commissions, Committees, and Similar Organizations), subchapter 1 (Compensation). Parole board members are not paid a salary. The members receive mileage and a $55 stipend for attendance at hearings.


V/r

Jenna Heald
Maine Department of Corrections
Policy & PowerDMS Assistant
FOAA Coordinator

title: Chatham County Police Department: Vendors Paid, FY2026 and FY2027 to Date (Chatham County Police Department)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Chatham County Police Department: Vendors Paid, FY2026 and FY2027 to Date (Chatham County Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A report or export from the County's financial system sufficient to show all vendors paid, or issued a purchase order, on behalf of the Chatham County Police Department for the most recently completed fiscal year (July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026) and for the current fiscal year (beginning July 1, 2026) through the date of this request. Please include the vendor name and, if the system maintains one, the vendor number. If the County's standard vendor or accounts-payable report already includes other fields, such as amounts paid, payment dates, purchase order numbers, or the department or cost center, please leave them in. I am not asking the County to create a new compilation.

This is a request for data fields in the County's financial database. Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(f), please provide it in the format in which it is kept or in a standard export format such as a CSV or Excel file.

If these records are held by the County's Finance or Purchasing Department rather than the Police Department, please forward this request to the appropriate department and let me know where it was sent.

Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1), any labor charge may not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee with the necessary skill and training, and the agency must use the most economical means reasonably calculated to produce the records. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis
communications.communication:
Dear Data Practices Compliance Official,

This is a formal request under the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (MGDPA), Minn. Stat. § 13.03, for public data regarding individual provider enrollment and agency affiliations within the Minnesota Provider Screening and Enrollment (MPSE) system.

1. Request for Remote Inspection

Under Minn. Stat. § 13.03, Subd. 3, I am exercising my right to inspect public data. As inspection is free of charge, I am requesting access to these records in the MPSE in their original digital format.

Reasonable Accommodation: Due to intersecting access barriers related to a qualified disability, I am requesting a reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II.

Strict adherence to a standard physical office environment creates a barrier to my access. Specifically, I require accessible system fonts and a specialized, non-standard ergonomic environment (including custom seating and positioning supports) to review materials at length. As these specific necessary environmental modifications are not feasible to replicate in a standard public government office on a shared terminal, I am requesting access to inspect the public data elements in situ with database tools remotely (via remote desktop, secure VPN, or a read-only digital portal).

This accommodation allows me to utilize my own adaptive workstation to review the material effectively and equitably.

This data is required for a public-interest analysis of provider retention. We are investigating whether a reported 250% turnover rate indicates that case managers are leaving the field before reaching the 24-month cadence of interactive disability-led training sessions with DHS partners, or if they are simply migrating between providers.

Data Requested

I am requesting access to a list of all individual case managers and providers enrolled to provide services at any point between January 2015 and December 2025, including the duration of their enrollment associated with each provider.

To facilitate an efficient remote inspection, please ensure a minimum of the following data points are accessible:

    Individual's Full Name

    Individual's State Provider Number (UMPI)

    Individual's National Provider Number (NPI)

    Agency Name (Employer) (Affiliation Records (MPSE-0603))

    Agency's Provider Number (NPI or UMPI) 

    Enrollment Start Date (per agency) (Enrollment History (MPSE-0604))

    Enrollment End Date (per agency; blank if currently enrolled)

If possible, I would like to be have access to the all public headers, fields and tables in the dataset  Along with the data dictionaries in order to facilitate accurate analysis.

Format and Collaboration

While I am requesting remote inspection to avoid the unnecessary fees and physical barriers, I would prefer to review this in a database. If that is infeasible a SQL dump or export to spreadsheet format (CSV or XLSX) or monthly snapshots similar to the NPI files would be an acceptably alternative allowing me to derive the needed relationships in the data.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

As this work is for a non-commercial, public benefit, I respectfully request a full fee waiver for any copies I may ultimately require after my initial inspection.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any of your team members are interested in our findings on churn rate, I would be more than happy to share the finished analysis.

Thank you for your assistance in ensuring this process remains accessible.

Best regards,

Sincerely,

Jonathan Murray | (Please use name/Any Pronouns) 
**Principal, Strategic Systems Innovation Lead, Social Infrastructure & Interdependence** 
* I run on Criptime so it may take a while to respond. Please follow up if I've missed your e-mail, especially if it's urgent.

communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

Following up on my MNDPA request and the request for payment for data access. 

The request specifically avoids asking DHS create new data, only for it to provide access to the public data in the databases segregated from information protected under the Minnesota Data Practices Act.

I understand the barriers that presents when the data is currently held within databases. I will need to use database tools either remotely or on on a MNDHS or MNIT machine.
The request offered of providing copies as a less burdensome way to comply with the obligations of the MNDPA in lieu of direct inspection.

I am reiterating my request to either have accessible remote access to the data directly or for copies to be provided free of charge. I am familiar with SQL and am happy to work with raw datasets and databases.

It's understandable that the DHS would like to avoid incurring costs. I believe providing access and working with me and others from the disability community to research the patterns the data will show, will greatly benefit the state of Minnesota through savings in case management & HCBS costs.

This isn't without precedent the Department of Health & DHS partnered with Elder Family Voices for related datasets and are providing ongoing technical support and data access for Elder Care IQ. https://eldercareiq.org/home

Elder care IQ is viewed as necessary because as "those vulnerable" we haven't had the agency, autonomy and authority ourselves to prevent abuses from happening to us and to stop them when they do. 

You can start to change that by taking this first step in partnering to create a disability lead and run disability data lab in MN. A place & platform on which  those of us who have already reached our disabled futures can work with Allies, Researchers, journalists, Policymakers and government officials all understand the disabled future we share. 

Until DHS buys into that vision. I would appreciate if you could provide access to the data free of charge as obligations under the MNDPA require.

Open roads and their skies,

Jonathan

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Leominster Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Gang Unit Policies & Database Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

1. Policies and General Orders: All current department policies, general orders, standard operating procedures (SOPs), special orders, training manuals, or memoranda governing the Joliet Police Department's identification, documentation, tracking, and validation of individuals as suspected gang members, associates, or affiliates.
2. Criteria Guidelines: Any documents detailing the explicit threshold criteria used by JPD officers or specialized units (e.g., Gang Unit, Special Operations Group) to determine whether an individual is entered into a gang database or designated as gang-affiliated (including criteria regarding tattoos, clothing, associates, social media, or self-admission).
3. Database Specifications: Records detailing the name, architecture, vendor, and system parameters of any local database, software platform, or intelligence system utilized by JPD to store gang affiliation data.
4. Data Sharing & Interoperability: All agreements, memorandums of understanding (MOUs), or policy documents detailing how JPD shares or receives gang-related data with outside entities (e.g., county sheriff's offices, Illinois State Police, federal agencies, or regional multi-jurisdictional intelligence centers).
5. Auditing, Oversight, and Removal: Any policies, guidelines, or logs concerning the periodic review, auditing, purging, or removal of individuals' names from JPD or shared gang databases, including any provisions allowing individuals to contest or appeal their designation.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

M

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: David Pollock (WINEP)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into former State Department official and scholar David Pollock (1950—9 January 2024). His death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, see his obituary from his employer, the Washington Institute for Near East Policy: https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/about/press-room/press-release/memoriam-dr-david-pollock

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: Deaths-in-custody (Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency)

communications.subject: Pennsylvania Right to Know Act Request: Deaths-in-custody (Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right to Know Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all Illinois law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant both Illinois state legislation (730 ILCS 210/3-5) and federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organizatin of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Carroll County Sheriffs Office)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Carroll County Sheriffs Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Carroll County Sheriffs Office.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Carroll County Sheriffs Office. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Carroll County Sheriffs Office, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Carroll County Sheriffs Office data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Carroll County Sheriffs Office policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Carroll County Sheriffs Office audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Carroll County Sheriffs Office personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Carroll County Sheriffs Office.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Carroll County Sheriffs Office.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Carroll County Sheriffs Office or by third party who make the information available to Carroll County Sheriffs Office. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Carroll County Sheriffs Office’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

title: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through August 19, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Christian Whitney

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)
communications.communication:
Thank you for the records produced on September 28 for PRA 26-446. I have downloaded the Dropbox materials.

Several items in my request were not addressed. The response did not produce records for them, state that none exist, or claim an exemption. Please provide a determination for each item below (Gov. Code § 7922.535). If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific exemption relied on (Gov. Code § 7922.540).

Flock audit and sharing records (Items 3, 4 and 5)
Please produce the following for the City of Lakewood's Flock account, covering the period from when the first cameras went live in June 2025 through when the account was deactivated:
  1. The Organization Audit log (all searches run against Lakewood's cameras by authorized users);
  2. The Network Audit log (all searches of Lakewood's data by other agencies);
  3. The Event Log, or equivalent record, of changes to settings, including network sharing, National Lookup, statewide lookup and hotlists;
  4. The network sharing export or list of agencies granted access, with the dates access was granted and revoked;
  5. Screenshots or exports of the hotlist configuration.

These records exist and the City has used them. The March 24, 2026 staff report (p. 6) describes an audit of data sharing that "Staff, with the assistance of Flock, recently conducted." It found that 15 out-of-state agencies and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service were granted access between mid-June and September 15, 2025. City emails show that Director Yordt asked Flock for a network audit on March 4, 2026. On March 8, 2026, Flock reported that it had "sent over the logs from June–September 2025 to Sgt. Johnson." Please produce those logs and the audit described in the staff report.

Format: please produce each log exactly as exported from Flock, as CSV or XLSX files. Please do not produce PDFs or printouts, merge files, delete columns or rename files. If any field is redacted, please redact only that field's contents, keep all columns, and cite the exemption for each redacted field. I request the logs unredacted, including plate numbers, search reasons and case numbers. Please see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032 on releasing system-level ALPR records.

Preservation: because the Flock pilot has ended and the cameras have been removed, I ask that the City export these logs from Flock now, and notify Flock to preserve them, while the City still has access to the account.

If the City's position is that any of these records are held only by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department or by Flock, please say so for each item. The City signed the Flock agreement and has stated that it owns the data, so records it can obtain from Flock remain within its possession. Please also assist in locating them (Gov. Code § 7922.600).

REMAINING ITEMS
  • SB 34 records (Item 6): the § 1798.90.52 access records and the results of any § 1798.90.53 audits, including the monthly audits by Lakewood Station noted in the March 24, 2026 minutes. Please also produce the equivalent search and audit logs from the Vigilant/LEARN system for the City's cameras.
  • Training, SOPs, misuse and impact reports (Items 9–11): please produce these, or confirm in writing that none exist.
  • January 2020 – May 2023 (Items 1–2): the production begins in May 2023. Please produce earlier Vigilant/Motorola contracts and communications, or confirm that none exist.
  • Non-use (Item 13): please confirm whether the City has used Peregrine, Palantir, Fusus or a similar platform.

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Fusus Audit Logs (Aurora Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Internal ALPR Activity report in Axon.

The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Axon's documentation, the Internal ALPR Activity report is available within the LPR > ALPR Search > LPR Audit menu. You can find instructions to locate this here: https://www.axon.com/help/fusus/software/fusus/alpr/alpr-audit.htm

2. Network ALPR Activity report in Axon.

The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Axon's documentation, the Network ALPR Activity report is available within the LPR > ALPR Search > LPR Audit menu. You can find instructions to locate this here: https://www.axon.com/help/fusus/software/fusus/alpr/alpr-audit.htm

3. ALPR Data Sharing report in Axon.

The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Axon's documentation, the ALPR Data Sharing report is available within the LPR > ALPR Search > LPR Audit menu. You can find instructions to locate this here: https://www.axon.com/help/fusus/software/fusus/alpr/alpr-audit.htm

4. ALPR Hotlist Management Audit report in Axon.

The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Axon's documentation, the ALPR Hotlist Management Audit report is available within the LPR > ALPR Search > LPR Audit menu. You can find instructions to locate this here: https://www.axon.com/help/fusus/software/fusus/alpr/alpr-audit.htm

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

title: Contract Request: SEDONA (California State University, Monterey Bay, College of Business)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Contract Request: SEDONA (California State University, Monterey Bay, College of Business)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Sedona Systems relating to the licensing of SEDONA to the College of Business at CSU Monterey Bay;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, data processing agreements, and/or letters of intent; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Sedona Systems for faculty information system technology;
and
Assessment documentation including, but not limited to, the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT). 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of SEDONA.

The scope of this request should encompass more than just direct contracts or renewals between the university and Sedona Systems; please incorporate all applicable agreements and supporting records facilitated through consortium entities (such as Lyrasis).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michele Gibney
