communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in Adair County. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions.

communications.subject: RE: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Douglas County Axon Logs (Douglas County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
Lisa,

The listed reasons for denial of records do not apply in this instance. Please proceed with the records request.

- CRS 42-4-110.5 refers only to automatic vehicle detection systems used to detect traffic violations, which does not apply to ALPR systems, nor their data.

- CRS42-4-110.5(7)(b) specifically refers to images and video, which I did not request. This is ultimately not relevant, as all of CRS 42-4-110.5 does not apply in this situation.

- CRS 42-4-110.5(7)(c) refers to photos, videos or personally identifiable information, which I did not request. Furthermore, per the Douglas County Sheriff Office's website: "ALPR specifically cannot track individuals or capture personal identifiers." And "This method deliberately avoids capturing unnecessary personal details and people."
(https://dcsheriff.net/sheriffs-office/government-transparency/use-of-technology-and-data/)
Again, this point is ultimately not relevant, as all of CRS 42-4-110.5 does not apply in this situation.

- CRS 24-72-305(5) allows for denial of the disclosure of records if such disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. I believe the release of these records is in the public interest. 

Per Douglas County Sheriff Office's website: "all use is subject to audit and oversight."
This should cover the 4 requested records: 
- Internal ALPR Activity Report
- Network ALPR activity Report
- ALPR sharing report
- ALPR Hotlist Management Audit Report

If there are individual redactions that need to be made for the public interest, then please do so. Otherwise, please proceed with the records request. 

Thank you,
William Beckett

communications.subject: RE: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Union Notices
communications.communication:
Dear Supervisor Arthur,

I write to appeal the Boston Public Health Commission’s (BPHC) denial of my public records request submitted on March 24, 2025, regarding union notices. BPHC has not complied with its obligations under G.L. c. 66 and 950 CMR 32.00, and I respectfully request that your office order the agency to conduct a reasonable search and produce responsive documents.

Request Summary

The request, submitted via MuckRock, is publicly available here:
https://www.muckrock.com/foi/boston-3/union-notices-183775/](https://www.muckrock.com/foi/boston-3/union-notices-183775/

It sought two specific categories of records:

1. “Copies of what your staff call ‘union notice’ in the last 12 months.”
2. Any policy documents that summarize when to notify unions.”

In follow-up clarification dated April 6, 2025, I further narrowed the request to high-level summary materials, internal guidance, or documents providing context about what union notices are and when they are issued.

 Agency Response

In its April 28, 2025 letter, BPHC:

Asserted that the request was “not a public records request” but instead a question,
Claimed the request was vague, overbroad, and unduly burdensome,
Declined to perform a search or offer any partial production,
Cited no exemption and provided no record or fee estimate.

 Basis for Appeal

 1. BPHC Has Previously Produced a “Union Notice”

BPHC has already acknowledged and produced this exact category of record in response to a prior public records request, publicly available at:
https://www.muckrock.com/foi/boston-3/727-shelter-179514/](https://www.muckrock.com/foi/boston-3/727-shelter-179514/

That response, provided without appeal, included a document described by BPHC as a union notice. The same Records Access Officer — Assistant General Counsel Javier Salas — handled both requests.

I have attached the previously disclosed “union notice” and the accompanying email in which BPHC staff explicitly refer to it using that term.

This prior disclosure demonstrates that:

 “Union notice” is a known and understood category of record within the agency;
 Responsive records clearly exist and have been disclosed in similar contexts;
The current claim of vagueness is not made in good faith.

2. The Request Seeks Clearly Identifiable Records

The request explicitly names a document type (“union notice”) and limits the timeframe to 12 months. It further narrows the scope to high-level or summary materials about a known union notification process.

Under 950 CMR 32.06 and relevant case law, an agency must interpret a request reasonably and make an effort to locate and provide any existing responsive records. Declining to conduct a search or even attempt a partial production fails to meet that standard.

3. The Denial Mischaracterizes the Request

BPHC’s position that the request was merely a “question” is contradicted by the plain language of the request, which explicitly asks for records. It is well-established that an agency may not avoid compliance by re-framing a valid record request as a question, especially where specific documents are described and requested.

 Requested Relief

I respectfully ask the Supervisor to:

1. Find that my March 24, 2025 request was a valid public records request under G.L. c. 66,
2. Order BPHC to conduct a search for responsive records and produce them on a rolling basis,  and
3. Remind BPHC of its duty to interpret requests reasonably and to respond in good faith 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please do not hesitate to contact me at this email address should further information be required.

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Flock/Axon HECVAT responses (The University Of Texas At Dallas)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) questionnaire, in any version (Lite, Full, On-Premise, or numbered 2.x, 3.x, or 4.x), completed by or on behalf of Flock Group Inc. d/b/a Flock Safety and held by this institution, whether received from the vendor directly or downloaded from the EDUCAUSE Community Broker Index or another repository. This includes any HECVAT covering, by any name, Flock's Falcon license plate reader cameras, Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Raven audio/gunshot detection, Condor video cameras, or Flock drone / drone-as-first-responder services (including Aerodome).
2. Any HECVAT questionnaire, in any version, completed by or on behalf of Axon Enterprise, Inc. and held by this institution, on the same terms. This includes any HECVAT covering, by any name, Axon Outpost, Fusus (Axon Fusus / Fusus ONE / Real-Time Crime Center), Axon Evidence (Evidence.com), Axon Body cameras, Axon Fleet in-car systems including Fleet ALPR, Axon Respond, Axon Records, Axon Air, Axon Standards, or Axon Investigate.

HECVATs are generally completed per product or solution, so a vendor may have submitted more than one; I request all of them. If no HECVAT exists for a vendor or product, please say so rather than treating the item as a nil response for the vendor as a whole.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

HCvP

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Garfield County Opioid Settlment Funding
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in Garfield County. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

communications.communication:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to Colin R. McMillan, who served as the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Production and Logistics from March 5, 1990, to December 11, 1992, under the George H.W. Bush administration.

Official Correspondence & Memoranda: Letters, policy directives, and briefing memos sent to or from Colin R. McMillan, including communications with then-Secretary of Defense Dick Cheney and/or former Secretary of Defense Frank Carlucci.
Calendar and Meeting Logs: Daily schedules, visitor logs, and agendas for his tenure (1990–1992).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Sincerely,

Charles Kallas

communications.subject: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: ALPR audit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Concerning Flock Safety, these files;

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

Typically the output for these audits is available in monthly batches.

3. A list of network share settings that include:
3a. Flock networks shared with me
3b. Networks that I’m sharing

4. All contracts concerning purchasing and installation for Flock Safety

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine readable format. For example, please provide csv or spreadsheet files where applicable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kansas City DSA
